memo:
Due to ongoing mental health services at the facility, construction noise and disruption cannot occur during business hours. Reconstruction must therefore occur after hours and on weekends, resulting in labor premium costs and extended mobilization requirements.

  

Once siding is removed, we expect to find additional damaged framing and wet materials. We will document and submit supplements as exposure continues.
termsAndConditions:
##[dsbudkjazwa20260202000005701] Insurance Coordination & Payment Terms – Reconstruction Phase

This estimate reflects the anticipated reconstruction work required following completion of mitigation activities related to the water intrusion incident. The scope and pricing presented are consistent with standard insurance reconstruction practices and are intended for submission to the Owner’s insurance carrier as part of the claim review and approval process.

The Owner acknowledges that insurance coverage and reimbursement determinations are made solely by the insurance carrier and that payment for reconstruction services remains the responsibility of the Owner regardless of insurance claim outcome. Golden Touch Remodeling will cooperate with reasonable documentation requests from the insurance carrier, including photographs, supplemental estimates, inspection access, and related reporting necessary to support claim processing.

Reconstruction work will proceed upon authorization by the Owner and insurance carrier where applicable. Payment for reconstruction services is due upon receipt of insurance funds or according to agreed progress payment terms. Any additional damage discovered during reconstruction that was not visible at the time of inspection will be documented and submitted to the insurance carrier as a supplemental request for approval prior to proceeding with additional repairs whenever practical.

termsAndConditions: Once it was discovered the toilet had leaked black water into the floor cavity and damage to the ceiling below was black water we removed the affected drywall. Plumbing connection in floor was to blame and due to other projects being in process, the plumbing needed to be replaced immediately in order to not cause excessive financial impact due to delays in timeline.

title: Judy Murphy
memo:
#[684txfrvpah20251115220018856] **Proposed Scope of Work for Judy’s Home Renovations**

*(Master Bathroom & Hall Bathroom)*

Golden Touch Remodeling is pleased to present the following summary of the improvements planned for your master bathroom and hall bathroom. Our goal is to refresh these spaces in a way that enhances comfort, safety, and everyday ease while giving your home a clean, updated feel. We’ve outlined everything in a simple, easy-to-understand format so you can feel confident about what to expect throughout the renovation.

  

##[ak16sbtmesu20251115220018857] **Master Bathroom**

To begin, your shower area will be updated with a new bypass-style shower door, with the final style and color selected together. We will be installing a chair-height elongated toilet for added comfort, as well as a new shower-trim kit and matching shower head. Once that trim is removed, we will also evaluate whether the internal cartridge should be replaced to ensure long-term reliability.

The flooring will be refreshed with new vinyl in a color of your choosing, and we’ll upgrade the bathroom exhaust fan to an ultra-quiet vent/heat model to help keep the space comfortable and reduce moisture.

In the vanity area, we will install a new countertop, new rectangular undermount sinks in white, and updated faucets. We will also install the new light fixture you’ve selected.

To complete the room, any necessary drywall repairs will be made, and paint will be touched up from corner to corner in the affected areas. New electrical outlets, switches, and water shut-off valves will be added so everything is up to date and functioning as it should. ***++In addition, four new recessed lights will be installed in the master bedroom, with the exact placement and lighting controls finalized together onsite to ensure they suit the space perfectly.++***

  

##[wga4m05drw920251115220018857] **Hall Bathroom**

The hall bath will undergo a full renovation designed to brighten the space and bring it up to modern standards. We will remove the existing tub and surround, vinyl flooring, toilet, countertop, mirror, and vanity light. The vanity itself will remain in place so new finishes can be installed around it.

A new standard-height bathtub will be installed, followed by a fully tiled tub surround. Tile color and style will be chosen together, and the design will include a convenient built-in niche on the back wall for toiletries. This bathroom will be designed for a shower curtain rather than doors. New plumbing fixtures for the tub and shower will be added as part of this upgrade.

We will replace the flooring with new vinyl, and a chair-height elongated toilet will be installed. The vanity will receive a new countertop with a 4" backsplash, a new sink, faucet, and a new vanity light fixture(client provided) . The bathroom fan will also be upgraded to an ultra-quiet model.

  

Drywall repairs will be completed as needed, and texture will be blended to match the existing walls. All electrical outlets and switches will be updated, along with new water shut-off valves at the plumbing connection points.

For the finishing touches, we will install new baseboards and reinstall the existing door trim if it is in good condition. Should the original trim be unusable, we will replace it with new material that matches the style of the updated bathroom.

title: AP Mental Health Water Mitigation
memo:
AP Mental Health

Vancouver, Washington, 98663

By Richard Lord

##[h7kt19xgr5n20260128163102357] Tue, Jan 27, 2026

Overview

WATER INTRUSION FIELD REPORT

  

  

AP Mental Health

Initial Investigation & Drying Log

Dates: January 24–27, 2026

  

  

1. Purpose of Visit

  

  

Site visit was initiated to remove a window in the back office area and perform minor cosmetic repairs in preparation for equipment installation. Upon removal of interior finishes, extensive water intrusion and structural deterioration were discovered, prompting immediate mitigation actions.

  

  

2. Discovery of Water Intrusion

  

  

After drywall removal around the window opening, the following conditions were observed:

  

  

Active water present inside the wall cavity

  

  

Standing water and ice in stud bays

  

  

Saturated insulation

  

  

Elevated moisture in framing members

  

  

Dry rot present in multiple locations

  

  

OSB sheathing biologically compromised

  

  

Car-deck style 2×6 roof structure saturated

  

  

Due to active moisture and deteriorated materials, additional openings were created to expose affected assemblies and follow the water intrusion path.

  

  

3. Source & Mechanism of Intrusion (Causation)

  

  

Inspection of the exterior flat roof area revealed:

  

  

A pony wall surrounding the roof was capped with segmented finger-joint wood pieces.

  

  

No waterproofing membrane or flashing was installed beneath the wood cap.

  

  

Wood cap joints exhibited movement and cracking, creating direct rainwater entry points.

  

  

Because the intrusion point was above the weather-resistive barrier, bulk water bypassed the sheathing layer and drained directly into the wall cavity.

  

  

This represents top-down water intrusion, a failure mode exterior gypsum sheathing cannot mitigate.

  

  

4. Wall Assembly Observations

  

  

Exterior walls were constructed using a legacy sheathing assembly consisting of:

  

  

Black-paper-faced gypsum exterior sheathing

  

  

Siding installed directly over the asphalt-impregnated facer

  

  

This product served as both sheathing and WRB historically, but it is not designed to resist bulk water from above. Resulting failures included:

  

  

gypsum core disintegration,

  

  

loss of facer integrity, and

  

  

transfer of moisture into adjacent framing members.

  

  

5. Structural Damage Observed

  

  

Documented deterioration included:

  

  

Extensive dry rot in pony wall framing

  

  

Compromised top plates of adjoining interior framing

  

  

Biological infestation throughout OSB sheathing layer

  

  

Moisture saturation in car-deck ceiling structure

  

  

Saturated insulation throughout affected cavities

  

  

At this time, exterior sheathing and compromised framing remain in place so the insurance adjuster can verify conditions and document biological infiltration and dry rot prior to removal.

  

  

6. Access & Exposure Scope

  

  

To follow the water path and expose affected materials:

  

  

100% of ceiling was removed in the back office space

  

  

20% of ceiling and wall was removed near rear entrance

  

  

All insulation was removed and disposed of

  

  

Exposed assemblies allowed accurate moisture assessment

  

  

Openings remain controlled to avoid unnecessary exposure of the interior to exterior moisture conditions prior to the adjuster’s visit.

  

  

7. Mitigation & Drying Actions

  

  

Following exposure:

  

  

All affected assemblies were treated with antimicrobial/antifungal agent

  

  

Drying equipment deployed from Jan 25 – Jan 27

  

  

Equipment Deployed

  

  

(1) Dri-Eaz commercial dehumidifier — 18 gallons/day

  

  

(3) Axial air movers — 1,000 CFM each

  

  

(1) HEPA air scrubber — continuous operation for duration

  

  

Projected removal scheduled for Jan 28, pending moisture verification.

  

  

8. Ambient Drying Conditions

  

  

Ambient Humidity: 37%

  

  

Temperature: 62–72°F

  

  

Conditions were within acceptable range for structural drying.

  

  

9. Moisture Content Log

  

  

Initial moisture readings taken immediately after exposure were unreliable due to standing water and ice (36–42%\+). Accurate baseline established after 12 hours of air movement and heat.

  

  

Detailed readings as provided by you are preserved without modification below:

  

  

Ceiling – Moisture Content

  

  

After 8 hrs: 19.6 | 17.5 | 16.8 | 16.9 | 22.4

Day 2: 17.8 | 14.6 | 13.6 | 15.4 | 18.5

Day 3: 13.8 | 12.6 | 11.3 | 10.4 | 9.1

  

  

Framing – Moisture Content

  

  

After 8 hrs: 24 | 18.6 | 30.5 | 32.8 | 18.6

Day 2: 15 | 14.8 | 15.9 | 22.2 | 17.2

Day 3: 21.4 | 11.5 | 12.6 | 17.9 | 12.4

  

  

Exterior Sheathing – Moisture Content

  

  

After 8 hrs: 16.3 | 27.3 | 33.6 | 23.7 | 42 | 23.7 | 19.9

Day 2: 14.1 | 21.2 | 28.5 | 20.2 | 35.6 | 19.8 | 15.4

Day 3: 13.6 | 14.2 | 16.5 | 18 | 13.7 | 12.2 | 19.2

  

  

Rear Door Area

  

  

After 8 hrs: 33.6 | 18.9 | 17.4 | 18.2

Day 2: 14.5 | 21.5 | 12.2 | 16.2

Day 3: 10.7 | 14.4 | 9.9 | 15.5

  

  

Inside Pony Wall – Stairwell Side

  

  

After 8 hrs: 22.7 | 24.8 | 19.6 | 15.9

Day 2: 19.4 | 18.5 | 14.4 | 12.2

Day 3: 14.2 | 13.9 | 10.4 | 11.6

  

  

10. Drying Objective & Status

  

  

Industry-standard drying objective for Douglas-fir framing members is:

  

  

≤15% Moisture Content prior to enclosure

  

  

As of Day 3, all monitored assemblies are trending below or near threshold. Based on current rate of decline, all areas are expected to reach target within 24 hours, allowing equipment removal on Jan 28 and transition to reconstruction scope.

  

  

11. Next Steps

  

  

Pending adjuster review on-site:

  

  

Remove biologically compromised sheathing

  

  

Remove compromised framing members

  

  

Identify replacement and reconstruction scope

  

  

Re-establish WRB and cap detail compliant with modern waterproofing standards
